title: Blueprint node: paths of Brownian motion are locally Holder of all orders below 1/2
intent: Record the blueprint node that turns three generic ingredients of the Kolmogorov-Chentsov argument — a cover of R+ with bounded covering numbers, the Kolmogorov condition for the pre-Brownian process, and the localized Hölder-modification theorem — into the headline fact that the paths of Brownian motion are locally Hölder continuous of every order below 1/2; the proof is the glue that instantiates those three nodes and computes sup_n (n+1)/(2n+4) = 1/2.

parent.name: lem:isHolderWith_brownian
parent.statement: The paths of the Brownian motion are locally Hölder continuous of all orders $\gamma \in (0, 1/2)$.

children.name: lem:isKolmogorovProcess_preBrownian
children.statement: The pre-Brownian process $X$ satisfies the Kolmogorov condition for exponents $(2n,n)$ with constant $(2n - 1)!!$ for all $n$: for all $s, t$, $\mathbb{E}[|X_t - X_s|^{2n}] \le (2n - 1)!! |t - s|^n$.
children.closed_by: its own proof (blueprint/src/chapters/brownian.tex 65-74), which cites lem:centralMoment_two_mul_gaussianReal (Gaussian central moments) and lem:hasLaw_preBrownian_sub (the increment law $X_t - X_s \sim N(0, |t-s|)$); formalised as ProbabilityTheory.isKolmogorovProcess_preBrownian

children.name: thm:localized_holder_modification_sup
children.statement: Let $T$ have a cover $(T_n)$ with bounded covering numbers (constants $c_n$, same exponent $d$); let $(p_n, q_n)$ be positive with $q_n > d$ and $X$ satisfy the Kolmogorov condition for $(p_n, q_n)$ for all $n$. Then $X$ has a modification $Y$ whose paths are almost surely locally Hölder continuous of all orders $\gamma \in (0, \sup_n (q_n - d)/p_n)$.
children.closed_by: its own proof (blueprint/src/chapters/kolmogorov_chentsov.tex 1840-1849), which cites thm:localized_holder_modification (the single-exponent version) and lem:indistinguishable_of_modification_of_continuous, then takes the sup over n; formalised as ProbabilityTheory.exists_modification_holder_iSup

applicability.goal_shape: A blueprint node stating a property of a canonically constructed object (here the Brownian motion $B$) that follows from a known universal theorem (the localized Kolmogorov-Chentsov modification) by choosing parameters; the proof is the instantiation glue plus a one-line computation of a sup.
applicability.use_when: the dependency graph already contains (a) a concrete cover of the index space with bounded covering numbers, (b) the process's Kolmogorov condition, and (c) a generic modification theorem parameterised by exponents; the node then exists only to record the instantiation (which $p_n, q_n, d$) and the arithmetic that yields the final order.
applicability.avoid_when: any of the three ingredients is not yet a named node; the sup computation is not elementary; or the process's Kolmogorov exponents cannot be pushed up by a uniform reindexing (here $n \mapsto n+2$ turns $(2n,n)$ into $(2n+4,n+2)$).

consequences: The node creates no new mathematical obligation: it is a pure instantiation of three already-proved nodes plus a sup computation, so its only consequence is a named fact (lem:isHolderWith_brownian) that lem:continuous_brownian cites (brownian.tex:124) and that definition def:brownian already foreshadowed (brownian.tex:78). Failure modes: the arithmetic step is mis-stated in the blueprint — line 112 writes '\leqslant 2' and 'tends to 2' where the correct bound is 1/2 (sup_n (n+1)/(2n+4) = 1/2) — so a reader copying the node verbatim must recompute the sup rather than trust that sentence. The instantiation also silently reindexes both ingredients: the cover T_n = [0, n+1) against the lemma's T_n = [0, n), and the Kolmogorov exponents (2n+4, n+2) against the lemma's (2n, n).
